newsitem.title: UK: Russia debt hits record highs as closing nears.
newsitem.headline: Russia debt hits record highs as closing nears.

text.p: Russian loans soared on Wednesday to set record highs on hopes its debt restructuring deal with the London Club of commercial bank creditors was edging closer to being finalized, traders and analysts said.
Analysts said market talk that Russia had fully reconciled up to 75 percent of its debt with creditors had led to the sharp gains. This compares with a figure of 60 percent last week.

"The latest figure circulating for the reconciliation of the London Club was around 75 percent and that has helped prices to firm," said Neil Lockwood, senior analyst at ANZ Investment Bank in London.
"The IANs and the PRINS are at all time highs," Lockwood added.
Russian IANs jumped 1-3/8 to set new highs of 80-1/4 bid and the country's PRINS rose 5/8 to trade at 72-3/8, just off its highs of 72-1/2 reached earlier today.
Brady bond dealers in London who trade Russian loans also said Russia was meeting with the London Club today and may propose lowering the limit needed to close the debt restructuring deal.
"Russia is going to the table today proposing to reduce the threshold to 75 percent from 90 percent," said a head Brady bond trader at a major U.S. investment bank.
He said the bank steering committee would be reluctant to lower the limit to 75 percent but might agree to an 80 to 85 percent critical mass.
Under current terms, Russia needs to fully reconcile 90 percent of the $24 billion principal of its total $35 billion debt owed to the London Club.
Bankers said officials from the London Club steering committee head Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Vneshekonombank and the ministry of finance were meeting on Wednesday to discuss the proposals.
In addition, traders said they were expecting Russia to announce the latest figure of debt that has been fully reconciled with the banks.
